sources.title: Andrew Gelman, John B. Carlin, Hal S. Stern, David B. Dunson, Aki Vehtari, and Donald B. Rubin, Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., Chapter 5
sources.locator: Author-hosted full PDF downloaded and inspected. Harvested Chapter 5 §§5.1–5.4 and §5.7 (printed pp. 101–119 and 128–132): hierarchical-prior construction, finite exchangeability, joint/conditional posterior factorization, normal random-effects shrinkage, current/new-group prediction, plug-in warning, and the improper log-scale variance-prior boundary.

contents.name: §5.1 Constructing a parameterized prior distribution
contents.support: The definition introduces a proper hyperprior and a common population kernel for group parameters; empirical-Bayes point estimation is kept distinct from the full joint posterior.

contents.name: §5.2 Exchangeability and hierarchical models
contents.support: The definition explicitly assumes a finite product-kernel hierarchy and records that arbitrary finite exchangeability alone does not imply a mixture-of-iid representation.

contents.name: §5.3 Joint, conditional, and marginal posterior distributions
contents.support: The theorem proves the local product-likelihood posterior formula with the exact positive-finite evidence condition and exceptional-fiber filler.

contents.name: §5.3 Drawing simulations from the joint posterior
contents.reason: The assigned pair proves the joint and conditional posterior laws but does not specify an MCMC, grid, or other posterior-simulation algorithm.

contents.name: §5.4 Conditional posterior of normal means with exchangeable parameters
contents.support: The theorem gives and proves the exact precision-weighted normal conditional posterior under positive known group-summary variances and positive between-group variance.

contents.name: §5.4 Posterior prediction for current and future groups
contents.support: The definitions distinguish conditioning on an existing group parameter from drawing a new group parameter from the posterior population kernel.

contents.name: §5.4 Substituting point estimates of hyperparameters
contents.support: The example computes a proper finite hyperposterior and proves that the full group posterior differs from the posterior at its hyperparameter mode.

contents.name: §5.7 Uniform prior on log tau and posterior impropriety near zero
contents.support: The example supplies a complete one-group Gaussian integral and a dyadic lower bound proving divergence for the improper log-scale variance prior.

contents.name: §5.7 Half-Cauchy recommendations and broader prior-sensitivity comparisons
contents.reason: The assigned design asks for an impropriety warning, not recommendations among weakly informative scale priors or a general prior-sensitivity analysis.

contents.name: §5.4 Normal location-scale density for conditional means
contents.support: The local lemma states the positive-variance normal density and proves it from the affine pushforward by change of variables.

sources.title: Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 15, Hierarchical Models are Exciting
sources.locator: Full official HTML chapter inspected; harvested §§15.1–15.4 and the chapter summary: complete pooling, no pooling, hierarchical data, partial pooling, and the limit on generalizing no-pooling fits to new groups.

contents.name: §15.1 Complete pooling
contents.support: The example identifies the common-mean boundary as the complete-pooling reference case.

contents.name: §15.2 No pooling
contents.support: The example identifies the group-only conditional mean and variance as the limiting no-pooling reference.

contents.name: §15.3 Hierarchical data
contents.support: The model definition names the population, finite group parameters, and within-group observations as separate probability layers.

contents.name: §15.4 Partial pooling with hierarchical models
contents.support: The example's algebra shows both local and population means receive strictly positive weight for every finite positive variance pair.

contents.name: §15.5 Chapter summary: pooling comparison
contents.support: The comparison is made precise by the example's exact finite-variance formula and separately stated boundary limits.

sources.title: Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 16, (Normal) Hierarchical Models without Predictors
sources.locator: Full official HTML chapter inspected; harvested §§16.3–16.6, including the normal hierarchy, hyperparameter layer, current/new-group posterior prediction, and shrinkage discussion.

contents.name: §16.3 Building the hierarchical normal model
contents.support: The model definition records within-group observation kernels, between-group parameter kernels, and a separate hyperprior layer.

contents.name: §16.3.2 Random-effects representation of group means
contents.support: The theorem's fixed-hyperparameter normal specialization matches the stated normal population law for group means.

contents.name: §16.4 Posterior analysis of global and group-specific parameters
contents.support: The page keeps the group conditional posterior separate from the posterior over shared global parameters; the library proof derives the exact conditional formula and then integrates over the full hyperposterior.

contents.name: §16.5 Posterior prediction for a current and an unobserved group
contents.support: The definitions reproduce the two distinct integrations: use an existing group's posterior parameter, or first draw a new group parameter from G_eta.

contents.name: §16.6 Shrinkage and the bias-variance trade-off
contents.support: The source motivates shrinkage toward the global trend; its approximate weak-prior weighted average is not imported as a general theorem, and the exact fixed-hyperparameter formula is proved locally.

contents.name: §16.3.3 Within- and between-group variance decomposition
contents.reason: The pair assumes known positive group-summary variances and proves conditional shrinkage; it does not assert the broader one-way ANOVA variance decomposition.

contents.name: §16.3 Normal within-group and between-group densities
contents.support: The chapter specifies the positive-variance normal kernels used in the hierarchy; the library lemma records their common location-scale density with a complete change-of-variables proof.
